briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 13, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Weather Grips the World and Its Severe Impacts
sections.content: According to news reported today, problems caused by heatwaves and droughts are intensifying across Europe, with extreme weather continuing as Spain approaches 40 degrees Celsius and the UK faces drought conditions [1, 221]. These climate changes are manifesting as a warning of 'climateflation,' halting navigation on the Rhine River and causing food prices to surge [3, 19]. The contiguous United States has also recorded its hottest month on record, highlighting a global phenomenon of abnormally high temperatures [210]. Notably, a report has also emerged stating that children today face seven times more extreme weather events than in the past, indicating that climate change threatens the lives of future generations [209]. Cases of nurses collapsing due to heatwaves clearly demonstrate the direct threat the climate crisis poses to humanity's basic living environment [222]. Furthermore, domestic awareness of the seriousness of climate change was recorded at 88%, but this is a 4 percentage point decrease compared to last year, indicating a moment when heightened vigilance is needed [20].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Drought Response and Climate Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, severe drought conditions persist, leading to emergency situations in the Gyeongnam region where military units and fire authorities are providing water supply assistance [201, 27]. In response, K-water is strengthening the tap water safety net through activated carbon self-sufficiency to combat heatwaves, droughts, and green algae blooms [17, 31], and the Korea Water Resources Corporation is also making all-out efforts to ensure drinking water safety [28]. Meanwhile, in the agricultural sector, adaptation efforts are active, including the development of 'Golden Ball,' an apple variety resilient to climate change, and calls for careful moisture management in farmlands [7, 8, 9, 14, 23]. The Northern Regional Forest Service is enhancing forest climate resilience by identifying broadleaf forests strong against climate change and establishing excellent afforestation sites [10, 12, 13, 26]. Gimhae City is also focusing on social adaptation, such as expanding support for climate-vulnerable groups affected by heatwaves [33].

sections.title: 🌱 Legislation of Carbon Neutrality Goals and Community-Led Efforts
sections.content: The National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate Crisis has passed an amendment to the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act, which legally specifies mid-to-long-term greenhouse gas reduction targets, setting goals of 69-80% reduction by 2040 and 84-90% reduction by 2045 [25, 34, 35, 74, 77, 85, 91, 97, 99, 105, 200]. Despite opposition from some environmental groups and concerns about the 'burden on future generations' [44, 47, 61, 75], the passage of this bill is a significant step forward, coming two years after the constitutional non-conformity ruling [56]. Local governments are actively pursuing carbon neutrality. Changwon Special City has been recognized as the top excellent case for carbon neutrality for two consecutive years and received the Minister of Climate's Commendation [38, 39, 40, 51, 72, 81, 83, 115]. Gwangmyeong City received the Gyeonggi Provincial Governor's Award for 'Gyeonggi Environmental Grand Prize' for its citizen-led carbon neutrality policies [36, 48, 54, 65, 87, 95, 96, 102]. Seocheon County also demonstrated outstanding performance, achieving 193.5% of its 2025 greenhouse gas reduction target [66, 84, 98, 111, 120].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Introduction of Innovative Models
sections.content: Efforts to expand renewable energy supply are accelerating nationwide. Yongin City has received the 'Excellent' rating for four consecutive years in the renewable energy supply project competition and plans to install new and renewable energy facilities, including solar power, at 134 locations by 2027 [121, 125, 127, 128, 129, 135, 139, 141, 142, 147, 152, 153, 157, 160, 162, 166, 169, 171, 172, 173, 174, 175, 176, 177, 180, 181, 183, 192, 194, 195, 196, 197, 198]. Notably, Paju City has become the first in the nation to complete a public renewable energy power plant on idle land at a water treatment plant, initiating a 'Direct PPA' model to directly supply electricity to local small and medium-sized enterprises [122, 123, 124, 131, 134, 136, 137, 140, 143, 148, 149, 150, 158, 161, 164, 165, 167, 168, 182, 185, 187, 189, 190, 199]. The government is promoting technological development, including tandem cells, super-large wind turbines, and next-generation power grids, to overcome the limitations of renewable energy [144, 145, 188]. Policy support is also being strengthened, such as easing regulations on the setback distance for solar and wind power generation facilities [132, 133, 146, 156]. However, concerns have also been raised regarding the indiscriminate installation of renewable energy facilities near national marine ecological parks and issues of rural destruction [126, 138, 159], emphasizing the importance of a balanced approach.

sections.title: ⚠️ The Dual Nature of AI Technology Development and Its Impact on Climate Change
sections.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is presenting new possibilities for responding to climate change. Domestically, research is underway to cultivate high-protein microalgae spirulina using AI in response to climate change [2]. Jeju National University also hosted a colloquium envisioning the future of AI power demand and carbon neutrality [50]. However, concerns are also growing regarding the negative impacts of AI technology development on climate change. Warnings have emerged that productivity improvements through AI could lead to increased oil and gas extraction, resulting in higher greenhouse gas emissions [155, 178]. Criticism has also been raised that companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, which are preparing for IPOs, remain silent on disclosing greenhouse gas emissions and presenting carbon neutrality targets [109]. Furthermore, an analysis suggests that climate change and AI are placing an increased burden on healthcare systems in the Asia-Pacific region [220], necessitating deep consideration for the sustainable development of AI technology.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has demonstrated that amidst the globally intensifying threat of extreme weather, policy and technological efforts for carbon neutrality and renewable energy expansion are being pursued concurrently both domestically and internationally. Recognizing the dual nature of AI technology and utilizing it wisely will be a crucial key to overcoming the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
